title: Coefficient ideal intersection for a split symmetric presentation
statement: Let $P$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq P$ an ideal, $A=P/I$, and $M=I/I^2$ projective over $A$. Let $m\geq0$ and let $q:A^m\to M$ be surjective. Put $C=\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. Let $\alpha:A[y_1,\ldots,y_m]\to C$ be an $A$-algebra map with $\alpha(y_j)=\iota(q(e_j))$, and let $\varphi:P[y_1,\ldots,y_m]\to C$ equal its composite with coefficient reduction $\pi$. Put $H=\ker\pi$ and $J=\ker\varphi$. Then $H\cap J^2=HJ$. The zero quotient ring and the empty variable set are allowed.

proof.text: Projectivity splits q, so M and ker(q) are finite projective direct summands of A^m. Take standard free covers of both modules and refine by pairwise products to obtain a common finite principal-open free cover. Lift each covering element of A to P.

On each nonzero member, choose bases adapted to A^m = M direct_sum ker(q). Symmetric-algebra base change and the free polynomial identification turn α into the projection A_a[u,v] → A_a[u]. Its kernel is generated by the complementary variables v; successive quotients remain polynomial rings and multiplication by the next variable is injective, so this is a regular sequence.

Apply the regular quotient intersection theorem with H ≤ J on each nonzero member to obtain H ∩ J² = HJ after localization. Exactness of module localization preserves intersections and quotients, and localization commutes with finite products of ideals. A zero member gives zero modules directly.

The quotient N = (H ∩ J²)/HJ is annihilated by J since J(H ∩ J²) ≤ JH, so it is a C-module and hence an A-module. Each standard localization of N vanishes. For x in N, choose a power of each covering element annihilating x; those powers generate the unit ideal, because a prime containing all the powers would contain all the covering elements. A unit-ideal linear combination shows x = 0. Thus N = 0 globally, proving H ∩ J² = HJ. If A = 0, H = J = Q, and the equality holds directly.

theorem projective_symmetric_coefficient_intersection
    (P : Type u) [CommRing P] (I : Ideal P) (m : ℕ)
    [Module.Projective (P ⧸ I) I.Cotangent]
    (q : (Fin m → P ⧸ I) →ₗ[P ⧸ I] I.Cotangent) (hq : Function.Surjective q)
    (α : MvPolynomial (Fin m) (P ⧸ I) →ₐ[P ⧸ I] SymmetricAlgebra (P ⧸ I) I.Cotangent)
    (hαX : ∀ j, α (MvPolynomial.X j) =
      SymmetricAlgebra.ι (P ⧸ I) I.Cotangent (q (Pi.single j 1)))
    (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin m) P →+* SymmetricAlgebra (P ⧸ I) I.Cotangent)
    (hφeq : φ = α.toRingHom.comp (MvPolynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))) :
    RingHom.ker (MvPolynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) (σ := Fin m)) ⊓
        (RingHom.ker φ) ^ 2 =
      RingHom.ker (MvPolynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) (σ := Fin m)) *
        RingHom.ker φ
